This first application has been filed by the applicant under Section 482 of Bharitya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant, who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No. 453/2024, registered at Police Station- Alot, District- Ratlam,
(M.P.) for offence punishable under Section(s) 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC.
As per the case of prosecution, Shyam Singh was working as Branch Manager of Spandana Sphoorty Financial Limited.

During audit of Spandana Sphoorty Financial Ltd. Branch - Alot Distt.
Ratlam(M.P.), it was revealed that the Loan Officer - Khushal Singh, the Loan Officer - Govind Mewada and Branch Manager - Shyam Singh had interpolated in the loan account of various customers of the company.
They sanctioned and foreclosed the loan account by using forged Aadhar Card and Voter ID and manipulated the accounts.

It was revealed that accused Shyam Singh misappropriated Rs.

Accordingly, P.S.- Alot registered FIR for offence punishable under Section 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC against Shyam Singh, Govind Mewada and Kushal Singh.
Accused - Shyam Singh was apprehended on 17.03.2025.
Govind Mewada and Kushal Singh were also arrested.
Relevant seizures have been made.

sentences.text: Manohar Singh and Gopal Singh(applicant) used to provide information with regard to bank passbook of family members.
Thereafter, on the basis of such information, he used to prepare forged aadhar card and voter ids'.
Govind Singh and Kushal Singh used to apply for group loan.

Thereafter,
the money was distributed amongst themselves.
The investigation is underway.
The applicant is apprehending arrest in the matter.
Learned counsel for the applicant in addition to the grounds submits that applicant is implicated in this matter merely on the basis of information given by Shyam Singh in police custody.
No incriminating material has been recovered till date.
No offence, as alleged, is committed by the applicant.

Co- accused Shyam Singh has been extended the benefit of regular bail vide order dated 16.04.2025 passed in M.Cr.C. No. 16018/2025 and co-accused Manohar Singh has been extended benefit of anticipatory bail vide order dated 28.04.2025, passed in M.Cr.C. No.18017/2025.
Applicant is aged 35 years.
He is an Agriculturist by profession.
Jail incarceration on false NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12223 3 MCRC-19450-2025 allegation would cause serious prejudice to the applicant.
He is ready to cooperate in the investigation.
Applicant may be extended the benefit of anticipatory bail.
Per Contra, learned counsel for the State opposes the application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Learned counsel further submits that investigation is underway.
Till date, except the information given by the co- accused - Shyam and Govind in police custody, no material is available implicating the applicant.
However, the custody of the applicant would be required for interrogation.
After going through the case diary, he fairly states that no criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.

Heard the arguments, perused the grounds for grant of anticipatory bail stated in the application,
case diary and the relevant material on record.
Allegedly, the applicant assisted the main accused Shyam Singh, Govind Singh and Kushal Singh in misappropriation of funds.
Shyam Singh has been extended benefit of bail.
The proseuction is based on documentary evidence and the statement of accounts.
There is no likelihood of tampering with evidence.
As informed, the applicant Gopal Singh is aged around 35 years.
He is an Agriculturist by profession and is sole bread earner of his family.
Considering the age, profession and status of the applicant, there appears to be no likelihood of fleeing from justice or involving in any criminal activity.

In absence of criminal antecedents, considering the socio-economic status of the applicant,
there appears to be no likelihood of tampering with the evidence, influencing the witness or interfering in the investigation by the applicant.
The grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant will cause no prejudice to free, fair and full investigation.

Considering his clean past, age, profession and future prospects, the applicant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:12223 4 MCRC-19450-2025 may suffer hardship and prejudice due to incarceration entailing social disrepute and humiliation.
Considering the overall circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the accusation, this Court is inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Thus, the application is allowed.
